rubric.why: A law is supported by repeated testing and has not been disproved.
rubric.description: States that a law has been repeatedly tested and not disproved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both ideas; accept equivalent wording.

rubric.why: A scientific law is a tested hypothesis or statement about nature.
rubric.description: Identifies a law as a hypothesis or scientific statement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a hypothesis or scientific statement.

modelAnswer: A law is a hypothesis or scientific statement that has been repeatedly tested and not disproved.

items.followUp: What is the function of ribosomes in a cell?

rubric.why: Lysosomes contain enzymes that digest materials.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their digestive enzymes or their digestion function.

rubric.why: Lysosomes digest materials inside cells, including worn-out parts and foreign particles.
rubric.description: States a role in intracellular digestion or removal of cellular materials.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example or the general role of intracellular digestion.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes and carry out intracellular digestion.
They break down worn-out cell organelles, cellular waste and foreign particles.

items.followUp: Give one reason why viruses are considered non-living outside a host cell.

rubric.why: Viruses lack cellular organisation and do not fit the cellular kingdom classification.
rubric.description: States that viruses are acellular or not made of cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the absence of cellular structure.

rubric.why: Viruses depend on host cells for reproduction and lack independent metabolism.
rubric.description: States that viruses cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism independently.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either dependence on a host for reproduction or lack of independent metabolism.

modelAnswer: Viruses are not included in any of the five kingdoms because they are acellular.
They cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism independently and multiply only inside a living host cell.

items.followUp: How does mitosis help in the growth of an organism?

rubric.why: Regeneration requires cell division to produce new cells.
rubric.description: Identifies mitosis or cell division as the process involved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming mitosis or cell division.

rubric.why: The new cells replace lost or damaged cells and help restore the body part.
rubric.description: Explains that new cells replace damaged or lost cells, enabling regeneration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the restorative role of the new cells.

modelAnswer: Mitosis produces new cells at the site of injury or loss.
These cells replace damaged or lost cells and help regenerate the body part.

items.followUp: Draw and label a diagram of metaphase of mitosis.

rubric.why: Anaphase is identified by separated chromatids moving towards opposite poles.
rubric.description: Shows the characteristic chromosome movement of anaphase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a diagram showing separated chromosomes or chromatids moving towards opposite poles.

rubric.why: Spindle fibres are a key structure to show and label in an anaphase diagram.
rubric.description: Includes a correct label for spindle fibres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly labelling spindle fibres; accept a clear label for poles as an equivalent diagram label.

modelAnswer: Draw an oval cell outline 8 cm long and 5 cm wide.
Mark one pole near each end of the oval; draw spindle fibres between the poles.
Draw separated V-shaped chromosomes moving towards opposite poles.
Label the chromosomes, spindle fibres and poles.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an acid and a base.

rubric.why: Oxidation can be described as addition of oxygen or loss of electrons.
rubric.description: Gives a correct definition or description of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any accepted description of oxidation.

rubric.why: Reduction can be described as removal of oxygen or gain of electrons.
rubric.description: Gives a correct definition or description of reduction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any accepted description of reduction.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen or the loss of electrons.
Reduction is the removal of oxygen or the gain of electrons.

items.followUp: What is the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Pigments absorb light, often at particular wavelengths.
rubric.description: States that pigments absorb light or particular wavelengths of light.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the light-absorption property.

rubric.why: Pigments appear coloured because they reflect some wavelengths of light.
rubric.description: Mentions the colour or wavelength-reflection property of pigments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pigments give colour or reflect other wavelengths.

modelAnswer: Pigments are coloured substances that absorb light of particular wavelengths and reflect other wavelengths.
